title: GATP Seminar – Geordie Williamson (Sydney)
desc: Intersection (co)homology is a beautiful invariant of singular spaces, e.g. singular complex algebraic varieties. Over the rationals it satisfies a raft of strong properties (e.g. Poincaré duality, hard Lefschetz, pure Hodge structure,…) which still seem like a miracle. In their paper introducing these groups, Goresky and MacPherson point out that (unlike the integral cohomology of smooth manifolds) it fails to satisfy Poincaré duality over the integers. Subsequent sheaf theoretic approaches have clarified the situation, and in fact one can prove that there is no reasonable theory over the integers which satisfies Poincaré duality. I will discuss intersection cohomology, given several simple examples that illustrate the theory. Then I will discuss work in progress with F. Klein and T.…

desc:
Title: Seasonal cycle of surface temperature: insights from simple models

Speaker: Joshua Duffield (Imperial)

Abstract: From the perspective of the annual harmonic, the role of surface heat capacity in controlling the seasonal cycle of surface temperature is readily apparent: a larger heat capacity leads to a greater lag (i.e., the time delay between peak incoming solar radiation and the hottest day of the year), as well as a reduced seasonal amplitude (i.e., the difference between summer and winter temperatures). Over the ocean, changes in heat capacity in response to global warming can therefore drive opposing amplitude trends. title: Dynamical Systems Seminar – Arthur Limoge
desc:
Speaker : Arthur Limoge

Title : The twist condition in the three-body problem

Abstract : A famous method for finding periodic orbits of dynamical systems, which we owe to Poincaré, is through fixed point theorems, most of which rely on some form of “twist condition”. In the case of the spatial (circular restricted) three-body problem, this twist condition is a geometric assumption on some 4-dimensional (symplectic) manifold. In this talk, I will describe a conjecture regarding this twist condition whose veracity would yield existence of infinitely many periodic orbits — an open problem to this day. This will be done with a minimum amount of technical details, so that the conjecture can be made accessible to people with little to no background in differential geometry or physics.

title: Finance and Stochastics Seminar – Tom Hadfield
desc:
Speaker : Tom Hadfield

Title : Patnaik-Pearson intrinsic dimension for internal representations of neural networks

Abstract : We define a new measure of intrinsic dimension of a data manifold, which we call the Patnaik-Pearson dimension, and apply this to internal representations of neural networks, in particular transformers. The inspiration for this comes from the HTSR and SETOL work of Martin, Mahoney and Hinrichs, combined with the TwoNN intrinsic dimension estimator of Facco et al. We prove various properties of this intrinsic dimension estimator. Treating weight matrices of neural networks as data manifolds, for weight matrices whose empirical spectral density follows a Pareto (power law) distribution, we relate the Patnaik-Pearson dimension to the HTSR and SETOL analysis and…

title: CCMI Seminar – George Stepaniants (University of Cambridge)
desc:
Speaker: George Stepaniants (University of Cambridge)

Title: A Shortcake Counterexample to the Planar Pompeiu and Schiffer Conjectures

Abstract: The Pompeiu and Schiffer conjectures are longstanding problems in integral and spectral geometry with deep connections to the theory of deconvolution and overdetermined eigenvalue problems arising in scattering theory and incompressible flows. We present a computer-assisted construction of a noncircular planar domain with real-analytic boundary that provides a counterexample to both conjectures, and discuss the implications of this result.

Abstract: This four-lecture series introduces variational inequalities to a general applied mathematical audience, pursues their finite element solution, and applies them to a geophysical problem. Variational inequalities are partial differential equation weak forms, but subject to bounds on their solution(s). They reformulate how one might pose boundary conditions at a free location; where the conditions apply is now determined simultaneously along with the solution.
